_comment: The three obfuscation tiers (paper §3.4, Table 2). They differ in how much of a tool's output a model could have seen during pre-training, and therefore in how much of the tier can carry controlled contrasts versus being reported as a wild condition. This file is the index; each tier's parameters live in its own config file.

open-source.role: Reproduces the legacy setting and carries the study's ablations: the only tier whose transformations can be enabled one at a time and whose builds regenerate from a recorded seed.

commercial.reproducible: build-time products only; online services are a wild condition
commercial.role: Contributes the three capabilities no build-time tool provides: runtime protection, usage/environment control, and per-build polymorphism. Reproducible products carry controlled contrasts; non-reproducible services enter as a wild condition sampled once and archived.

model-generated.reproducible: yes, from a pinned model snapshot + prompts (released as artifacts)
model-generated.role: A control against memorization: the model chooses the realization, so the transformation space is open-ended and cannot have been seen during pre-training. Also the only tier that makes polymorphism releasable, since repeated generation yields distinct builds that can be archived.

admission._comment: Every build in every tier passes the same check before entering builds.jsonl: it and the original are run against the subject's workload in the sandbox and their observable behavior compared; divergent builds are discarded and recorded. Implemented for the open-source tier in scripts/02_admit.py, reused by the other tiers.
admission.mechanism: sandbox/scripts/score.py (differential test) for subjects with a usable oracle; interface-level export comparison (L1) otherwise
admission.environment_conditional: Domain-lock and self-defending builds are deliberately not semantics-preserving; admission configures the sandbox to satisfy a build's declared environment, and records every build discarded on this ground instead of dropping it silently.

reporting._comment: For each admitted build the pipeline reports size inflation and a structural complexity score (tools/complexity.mjs), so tiers are compared on measured strength rather than on tool names.
